name: CULTURE SENSITIVITY- SPUTUM
description: Sputum Culture & Sensitivity identifies respiratory pathogens and determines antibiotic susceptibility. This test diagnoses lower respiratory tract infections and guides targeted antimicrobial therapy.

testdeatils.method: Conventional Culture with Antibiotic Susceptibility Testing
testdeatils.instrumentation: Automated Culture Systems (BD BACTEC, bioMérieux VITEK)

literatureReview: Sputum Culture & Sensitivity diagnoses bacterial pneumonia and other lower respiratory tract infections. Quality specimen required - deep cough, >25 squamous epithelial cells and <10 neutrophils per low power field indicates good quality. Common pathogens: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Legionella. Inoculated onto blood agar, chocolate agar, MacConkey agar. Incubated in CO2. Gram stain performed for preliminary identification. Antibiotic susceptibility testing guides therapy. Critical for hospital-acquired pneumonia and immunocompromised patients. TAT 24-72 hours. Negative culture doesn't rule out infection if prior antibiotics given or specimen poor quality.
